label: original-phase input from {x,v,1,y,e,q,c,t,m,a} after >=2 earlier {r,b,2,p,l,z,k,g,3,h} tokens
explanation: Mostly an original-phase unit (95% of activation mass), peaking at positions 3-6 and never active at t=0. Two things drive it together: the current input is one of x, v, 1, y, e, q (also c, t, m, a; x is strongest at 22% rate), and the earlier tokens in the sequence come from a second set: r, b, 2, p, l, z, k, g, 3, h. That second set shows up as high lift for first_tok and prev2_tok. The largest activations look like "r r g 3 q [x]" or "b b b y [x]": a run of set-A tokens followed by x or v. It rarely fires during the copy phase or on <DEL>, which hold small leftover activation (about 5% of mass), and it rarely fires on repeated tokens (in_first=0). The same x/v/1 inputs mostly stay silent when the earlier tokens are vowels or other letters (u, e, x, c, f, s, ...). The dependence is graded, like a linear readout of hidden state, so a boolean predicate tops out near F1 0.5. Dev scores: precision 0.53, recall 0.48, mass recall 0.64, with better coverage of the top activation quartile.
